procedure_signatures.notes: Batch 4I skill 4/5. Owns the dot product AS A PROJECTION TOOL: the component form A . B = Ax Bx + Ay By + Az Bz, the geometric form A . B = |A||B| cos theta, and the signed SCALAR projection of A onto the direction of B, A_par = (A . B)/|B|, including what a negative projection means (obtuse theta; A has a component opposite to B). Boundary: cartesian_vector_components_3d (signed parent) supplies components, cited not re-derived. RECIPROCAL BOUNDARY with cross_product_moment_3d (signed earlier this batch) is stated in the artifact: that skill uses a dot product ONLY as a perpendicularity check and computes no projection, while this skill owns the dot product as a projection tool and computes no moment or cross product - naming the complement was required because the sibling already states its half. unit_vector_along_line (downstream, planned) owns FORMING a unit direction; this skill uses the general form (A . B)/|B|, which needs no unit vector, and never binds or constructs one. The VECTOR projection (scalar times a unit direction) therefore requires that ceded construction and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE - the deliverable is the signed SCALAR projection. position_vector_3d, coordinate_direction_angles and cartesian_vector_addition_3d excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived from the on-disk prompt: A = -6i -6j -3k (|A| = 9), B = 2i +2j -1k (|B| = 3); A . B = (-6)(2) + (-6)(2) + (-3)(-1) = -12 - 12 + 3 = -21; A_par = -21/3 = -7; cos theta = -21/27 = -7/9 = -0.7778 -> theta = 141.1 deg. Distinguishing feature bites: the geometry is neither parallel nor perpendicular and theta sits clear of both 90 and 180 degrees; the projection is NEGATIVE so its sign carries meaning and the obtuse angle explains it; |A| != |B| so dividing by the wrong magnitude is detectable; and the four outcomes are mutually distinct - correct -7, wrong denominator -2.33, undivided -21, signs dropped +9 - so each mapped signal routes to its own answer. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays (verify at index 5, report at index 6), matching the three skills signed earlier in this batch: the bound |A_par| < |A|, valid because A and B are not parallel, gives 7 < 9. HONEST LIMITATION recorded: the bound catches an undivided product sum (21 > 9) and a sign-dropped product sum (27/3 = 9, not strictly less than 9) but does NOT catch dividing by |A| instead of |B| (2.33 < 9 passes while being wrong) - stated as a property of the check rather than overstated. THREE-signal mapping: axis_confusion at step 2 (like-component pairing in the product sum - multiplying Ax by By or Az by Bx), sign_or_placement_error at step 3 (sign retention through the division AND selection of |B| rather than |A| as the divisor, since dividing by |A| projects the wrong way round and is a placement error about which vector is the direction; both acts are explicitly authored in that step, distinct from the pairing act at step 2), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - incomplete result, omitted sign, skipped bound check, treating the bound as catching a wrong-denominator error, forming a unit vector or vector projection, or reaching into the ceded siblings). solution_sequencing_error OMITTED with explicit argument: A . B and |B| are independent computations combined by one division, so no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown; it was not mapped merely because the division follows the dot product. simple_average_used omitted (Centroids-family). Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: components are given already resolved and no inclined vector is decomposed. NO ARCHETYPE IS ASSERTED for this skill: the Architect flagged its family fit for independent review and directed that it not be forced into a component-combination template, so the artifact carries no archetype reference and the assignment is deferred to PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 review. Operator observation recorded, not corrected: the bound-check step cites a sign-dropped sum of 27 without restating that 27 is the sum of the product magnitudes from two steps earlier - terse but inferable, and the instructional point of the sentence lands. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane.

Batch 4E skill 3/6 — opens the 3D chain. SCOPE WAS OPERATOR-DERIVED, not Architect-ruled: the Batch 4E ruling detailed skill 1/6's scope only. Derived from graph truth and the signed boundaries. The Architect's binding 3D ruling was honored: this is particle-equilibrium debt retirement, not 3D rigid-body expansion — no rigid_body_fbd_3d, no 3D rigid-body equilibrium. Narrow by construction: one force in, three components out. Every adjacent capability is a separate graph node and none appears as an authored step — coordinate direction angles, 3D vector addition, position vectors, unit vectors along a line, dot and cross products, 3D FBDs, and equilibrium are all excluded, and step 7 names them explicitly. Boundary against the signed solve_particle_equil_3d (downstream; its unsigned-prereq inversion is retired by skill 4/6, not this one) verified at the review beat: that skill's worked example HANDS the student unit vectors and writes SumF = 0; it consumes 3D components without ever teaching the two-angle projection geometry. Boundary against the parent vector_components_2d: that skill is one angle into two components; this one requires TWO angular data and produces three nonzero components. Worked example independently re-derived by Operator: F = 100 N, phi = 36.9 degrees from +z (cos 0.80, sin 0.60), xy-projection at theta = 53.1 degrees from +x into the +x/-y region (cos 0.60, sin 0.80); F_xy = 60 N, Fz = 80 N, Fx = +36 N, Fy = -48 N, giving F = 36 i - 48 j + 80 k N. All three components nonzero. Magnitude check closes exactly: 1296 + 2304 + 6400 = 10000 = 100 squared. 3-signal mapping, content-earned: axis_confusion at step 3 (the out-of-plane projection — this skill's own 3D contribution, since the parent has no such step); sign_or_placement_error at step 5 (assigning algebraic signs, genuinely distinct from the resolution steps: correct magnitudes, wrong sense); unclassified at step 7 (verification and scope boundary). simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. HONEST FINDING, recorded because it is a real property of the verification step: a clean sine/cosine swap PRESERVES the magnitude check, because it permutes which axis receives which magnitude — the swap at phi gives 48/-64/60 and the swap at theta gives 48/-36/80, and both close to 10000. The magnitude relation catches dropped or mis-scaled components, not a clean trig swap; axis_confusion is what routes the swap, and the procedure does not claim otherwise. Procedure step 4 (the in-plane split) is deliberately LEFT UNMAPPED: that is vector_components_2d's content, and a student failing there needs the parent skill, which already diagnoses it — the same principle applied on support_reactions_2d. SIGNAL-POLICY DEBT recorded per Architect Batch 4E Decision B: a theta-swap at step 4 yields (48, -36, 80), which is wrong AND closes the magnitude check, so no signal on this skill catches it. Mapping a duplicate axis_confusion there is forbidden by Decision B, and inventing a signal is not authorized; the hole is recorded rather than forced. Review-beat correction: the draft used alpha for the angle from +z while common_errors warned students against the coordinate direction angles alpha/beta/gamma — but those are conventionally measured from +x/+y/+z, so the angle this skill called alpha is conventionally gamma. The artifact was using a coordinate-direction-angle symbol for a different meaning while telling students that convention belongs elsewhere, and coordinate_direction_angles is a downstream node this skill unlocks, where alpha will mean angle-from-+x. Renamed to phi, the standard polar angle from +z, which pairs conventionally with theta azimuthal. Alpha now survives only inside the literal string alpha/beta/gamma where it correctly names the other skill's convention. Numbers, components, answer, step count, and signal targets all unchanged by the rename. PROCESS NOTE: the correction lane BLOCKED on a defective Operator verification gate that compared a six-character slice against a five-character string and therefore could never pass. Cursor refused to edit content to satisfy it and escalated with a diagnosis — the correct call, and the standing rule.

signed_procedure_steps: Identify the given Cartesian vectors A (to be projected) and B (direction). Cite cartesian_vector_components_3d for components. Do not form a unit direction, a position vector, direction angles, a resultant by addition, a moment, or a cross product.
Pair like components and form the product sum A · B = Ax Bx + Ay By + Az Bz. Do not multiply across axes (Ax with By, for example).
Compute |A| and |B|. Form the signed scalar projection A_par = (A · B) / |B|, retaining the algebraic sign of A · B and using |B| — not |A| — as the divisor.
Recover cos θ = (A · B) / (|A| |B|) and θ. A negative A_par means θ is obtuse and A has a component opposite to B.

Verify before reporting: if A and B are not parallel, confirm |A_par| < |A|. This bound catches an undivided product sum and a sign-dropped product sum that is not strictly less than |A|; it does not catch dividing by |A| instead of |B|.
Report A_par (signed scalar projection) and θ. Do not report a vector projection.
Stop. Do not form a unit vector, a vector projection, a moment, a cross product, a position vector, direction angles, or a resultant by addition.

Pair like components and form the product sum A · B = Ax Bx + Ay By + Az Bz. Do not multiply across axes (Ax with By, for example).
Compute |A| and |B|. Form the signed scalar projection A_par = (A · B) / |B|, retaining the algebraic sign of A · B and using |B| — not |A| — as the divisor.
Recover cos θ = (A · B) / (|A| |B|) and θ. A negative A_par means θ is obtuse and A has a component opposite to B.

Verify before reporting: if A and B are not parallel, confirm |A_par| < |A|. This bound catches an undivided product sum and a sign-dropped product sum that is not strictly less than |A|; it does not catch dividing by |A| instead of |B|.
Report A_par (signed scalar projection) and θ. Do not report a vector projection.
Stop. Do not form a unit vector, a vector projection, a moment, a cross product, a position vector, direction angles, or a resultant by addition.

procedure_signatures.notes: Batch 4I skill 4/5. Owns the dot product AS A PROJECTION TOOL: the component form A . B = Ax Bx + Ay By + Az Bz, the geometric form A . B = |A||B| cos theta, and the signed SCALAR projection of A onto the direction of B, A_par = (A . B)/|B|, including what a negative projection means (obtuse theta; A has a component opposite to B). Boundary: cartesian_vector_components_3d (signed parent) supplies components, cited not re-derived. RECIPROCAL BOUNDARY with cross_product_moment_3d (signed earlier this batch) is stated in the artifact: that skill uses a dot product ONLY as a perpendicularity check and computes no projection, while this skill owns the dot product as a projection tool and computes no moment or cross product - naming the complement was required because the sibling already states its half. unit_vector_along_line (downstream, planned) owns FORMING a unit direction; this skill uses the general form (A . B)/|B|, which needs no unit vector, and never binds or constructs one. The VECTOR projection (scalar times a unit direction) therefore requires that ceded construction and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE - the deliverable is the signed SCALAR projection. position_vector_3d, coordinate_direction_angles and cartesian_vector_addition_3d excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived from the on-disk prompt: A = -6i -6j -3k (|A| = 9), B = 2i +2j -1k (|B| = 3); A . B = (-6)(2) + (-6)(2) + (-3)(-1) = -12 - 12 + 3 = -21; A_par = -21/3 = -7; cos theta = -21/27 = -7/9 = -0.7778 -> theta = 141.1 deg. Distinguishing feature bites: the geometry is neither parallel nor perpendicular and theta sits clear of both 90 and 180 degrees; the projection is NEGATIVE so its sign carries meaning and the obtuse angle explains it; |A| != |B| so dividing by the wrong magnitude is detectable; and the four outcomes are mutually distinct - correct -7, wrong denominator -2.33, undivided -21, signs dropped +9 - so each mapped signal routes to its own answer. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays (verify at index 5, report at index 6), matching the three skills signed earlier in this batch: the bound |A_par| < |A|, valid because A and B are not parallel, gives 7 < 9. HONEST LIMITATION recorded: the bound catches an undivided product sum (21 > 9) and a sign-dropped product sum (27/3 = 9, not strictly less than 9) but does NOT catch dividing by |A| instead of |B| (2.33 < 9 passes while being wrong) - stated as a property of the check rather than overstated. Batch 4E skill 3/6 — opens the 3D chain. SCOPE WAS OPERATOR-DERIVED, not Architect-ruled: the Batch 4E ruling detailed skill 1/6's scope only. Derived from graph truth and the signed boundaries. The Architect's binding 3D ruling was honored: this is particle-equilibrium debt retirement, not 3D rigid-body expansion — no rigid_body_fbd_3d, no 3D rigid-body equilibrium. Narrow by construction: one force in, three components out. Every adjacent capability is a separate graph node and none appears as an authored step — coordinate direction angles, 3D vector addition, position vectors, unit vectors along a line, dot and cross products, 3D FBDs, and equilibrium are all excluded, and step 7 names them explicitly. Boundary against the signed solve_particle_equil_3d (downstream; its unsigned-prereq inversion is retired by skill 4/6, not this one) verified at the review beat: that skill's worked example HANDS the student unit vectors and writes SumF = 0; it consumes 3D components without ever teaching the two-angle projection geometry. Boundary against the parent vector_components_2d: that skill is one angle into two components; this one requires TWO angular data and produces three nonzero components. Worked example independently re-derived by Operator: F = 100 N, phi = 36.9 degrees from +z (cos 0.80, sin 0.60), xy-projection at theta = 53.1 degrees from +x into the +x/-y region (cos 0.60, sin 0.80); F_xy = 60 N, Fz = 80 N, Fx = +36 N, Fy = -48 N, giving F = 36 i - 48 j + 80 k N. All three components nonzero. Magnitude check closes exactly: 1296 + 2304 + 6400 = 10000 = 100 squared. 3-signal mapping, content-earned: axis_confusion at step 3 (the out-of-plane projection — this skill's own 3D contribution, since the parent has no such step); sign_or_placement_error at step 5 (assigning algebraic signs, genuinely distinct from the resolution steps: correct magnitudes, wrong sense); unclassified at step 7 (verification and scope boundary). simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. Procedure step 4 (the in-plane split) is deliberately LEFT UNMAPPED: that is vector_components_2d's content, and a student failing there needs the parent skill, which already diagnoses it — the same principle applied on support_reactions_2d. SIGNAL-POLICY DEBT recorded per Architect Batch 4E Decision B: a theta-swap at step 4 yields (48, -36, 80), which is wrong AND closes the magnitude check, so no signal on this skill catches it. Mapping a duplicate axis_confusion there is forbidden by Decision B, and inventing a signal is not authorized; the hole is recorded rather than forced. Review-beat correction: the draft used alpha for the angle from +z while common_errors warned students against the coordinate direction angles alpha/beta/gamma — but those are conventionally measured from +x/+y/+z, so the angle this skill called alpha is conventionally gamma. The artifact was using a coordinate-direction-angle symbol for a different meaning while telling students that convention belongs elsewhere, and coordinate_direction_angles is a downstream node this skill unlocks, where alpha will mean angle-from-+x. Renamed to phi, the standard polar angle from +z, which pairs conventionally with theta azimuthal. Alpha now survives only inside the literal string alpha/beta/gamma where it correctly names the other skill's convention. Numbers, components, answer, step count, and signal targets all unchanged by the rename. RECIPROCAL BOUNDARY with cross_product_moment_3d (signed earlier this batch) is stated in the artifact: that skill uses a dot product ONLY as a perpendicularity check and computes no projection, while this skill owns the dot product as a projection tool and computes no moment or cross product - naming the complement was required because the sibling already states its half. unit_vector_along_line (downstream, planned) owns FORMING a unit direction; this skill uses the general form (A . B)/|B|, which needs no unit vector, and never binds or constructs one. The VECTOR projection (scalar times a unit direction) therefore requires that ceded construction and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE - the deliverable is the signed SCALAR projection. position_vector_3d, coordinate_direction_angles and cartesian_vector_addition_3d excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived from the on-disk prompt: A = -6i -6j -3k (|A| = 9), B = 2i +2j -1k (|B| = 3); A . B = (-6)(2) + (-6)(2) + (-3)(-1) = -12 - 12 + 3 = -21; A_par = -21/3 = -7; cos theta = -21/27 = -7/9 = -0.7778 -> theta = 141.1 deg. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays (verify at index 5, report at index 6), matching the three skills signed earlier in this batch: the bound |A_par| < |A|, valid because A and B are not parallel, gives 7 < 9. Batch 4E skill 3/6 — opens the 3D chain. SCOPE WAS OPERATOR-DERIVED, not Architect-ruled: the Batch 4E ruling detailed skill 1/6's scope only. Derived from graph truth and the signed boundaries. The Architect's binding 3D ruling was honored: this is particle-equilibrium debt retirement, not 3D rigid-body expansion — no rigid_body_fbd_3d, no 3D rigid-body equilibrium. Narrow by construction: one force in, three components out. Every adjacent capability is a separate graph node and none appears as an authored step — coordinate direction angles, 3D vector addition, position vectors, unit vectors along a line, dot and cross products, 3D FBDs, and equilibrium are all excluded, and step 7 names them explicitly. Boundary against the signed solve_particle_equil_3d (downstream; its unsigned-prereq inversion is retired by skill 4/6, not this one) verified at the review beat: that skill's worked example HANDS the student unit vectors and writes SumF = 0; it consumes 3D components without ever teaching the two-angle projection geometry. Boundary against the parent vector_components_2d: that skill is one angle into two components; this one requires TWO angular data and produces three nonzero components. Worked example independently re-derived by Operator: F = 100 N, phi = 36.9 degrees from +z (cos 0.80, sin 0.60), xy-projection at theta = 53.1 degrees from +x into the +x/-y region (cos 0.60, sin 0.80); F_xy = 60 N, Fz = 80 N, Fx = +36 N, Fy = -48 N, giving F = 36 i - 48 j + 80 k N. All three components nonzero. Magnitude check closes exactly: 1296 + 2304 + 6400 = 10000 = 100 squared. 3-signal mapping, content-earned: axis_confusion at step 3 (the out-of-plane projection — this skill's own 3D contribution, since the parent has no such step); sign_or_placement_error at step 5 (assigning algebraic signs, genuinely distinct from the resolution steps: correct magnitudes, wrong sense); unclassified at step 7 (verification and scope boundary). simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. Procedure step 4 (the in-plane split) is deliberately LEFT UNMAPPED: that is vector_components_2d's content, and a student failing there needs the parent skill, which already diagnoses it — the same principle applied on support_reactions_2d. SIGNAL-POLICY DEBT recorded per Architect Batch 4E Decision B: a theta-swap at step 4 yields (48, -36, 80), which is wrong AND closes the magnitude check, so no signal on this skill catches it. Mapping a duplicate axis_confusion there is forbidden by Decision B, and inventing a signal is not authorized; the hole is recorded rather than forced. Review-beat correction: the draft used alpha for the angle from +z while common_errors warned students against the coordinate direction angles alpha/beta/gamma — but those are conventionally measured from +x/+y/+z, so the angle this skill called alpha is conventionally gamma. The artifact was using a coordinate-direction-angle symbol for a different meaning while telling students that convention belongs elsewhere, and coordinate_direction_angles is a downstream node this skill unlocks, where alpha will mean angle-from-+x. Renamed to phi, the standard polar angle from +z, which pairs conventionally with theta azimuthal. Alpha now survives only inside the literal string alpha/beta/gamma where it correctly names the other skill's convention. Numbers, components, answer, step count, and signal targets all unchanged by the rename. signed_procedure_steps: Identify the given Cartesian vectors A (to be projected) and B (direction). Cite cartesian_vector_components_3d for components. Do not form a unit direction, a position vector, direction angles, a resultant by addition, a moment, or a cross product.
Pair like components and form the product sum A · B = Ax Bx + Ay By + Az Bz. Do not multiply across axes (Ax with By, for example).
Compute |A| and |B|. Form the signed scalar projection A_par = (A · B) / |B|, retaining the algebraic sign of A · B and using |B| — not |A| — as the divisor.
Recover cos θ = (A · B) / (|A| |B|) and θ. A negative A_par means θ is obtuse and A has a component opposite to B.

Verify before reporting: if A and B are not parallel, confirm |A_par| < |A|. This bound catches an undivided product sum and a sign-dropped product sum that is not strictly less than |A|; it does not catch dividing by |A| instead of |B|.
Report A_par (signed scalar projection) and θ. Do not report a vector projection.
Stop. Do not form a unit vector, a vector projection, a moment, a cross product, a position vector, direction angles, or a resultant by addition.

Take u_AB as given or cite its construction from r_AB and |r_AB|; do not re-derive normalization as the objective. Do not project a vector onto a direction (dot_product_projection). Do not form a moment. Do not write equilibrium equations or a reaction inventory.

Obtain u_AB for the stated FROM-A-TO-B direction. Form the force components by multiplying F by each unit-vector component on matching axes only: F_x with the x-component of u_AB, F_y with the y-component, F_z with the z-component. Do not transpose components between axes or pair F with a mismatched unit-vector component.

Assemble F_vec = F u_AB. Confirm the direction matches the stated tail and head. Form the reversed-order contrast: u_BA = −u_AB gives F u_BA = −F_vec — every component negated. Record that the point order is part of the answer.

Verify before reporting by a route that does not reuse the multiplication: compute |F_vec| from its components and confirm it equals F; also confirm F_vec / F recovers u_AB. Record that the magnitude check cannot detect a reversed point order and does not validate the given F or the endpoint coordinates.
Report F_vec with units and the stated tail and head (FROM A TO B). Stop.

work_by_step.work: State F=534.976635 N FROM A=(121, 144, 167) TO B=(111, 131, 160); cite unit_vector_along_line.
F_vec=(-300.0, -390.0, -210.0) N; reversed order negates every component.
Independent check |F_vec|=534.976635 N and F_vec/F recovers u_AB.
Report F_vec=(-300.0, -390.0, -210.0) N FROM A TO B and stop.

procedure_signatures.notes: Force of known magnitude directed along a line expressed as a Cartesian vector, F_vec = F u_AB. Independently re-derived: |r_AB| = sqrt(16 + 144 + 9) = sqrt(169) = 13 m; u_AB = (4/13, -12/13, 3/13), mixed sign on all three axes; 390 / 13 = 30 exactly, so F_vec = (120, -360, 90) N, whose components are clean integers visibly distinct from the unit-vector fractions so that the unit vector cannot be mistaken for the force. Verified by a route independent of the multiplication: |F_vec| = sqrt(14400 + 129600 + 8100) = sqrt(152100) = 390 N, recovering the given scalar, and F_vec / 390 = (4/13, -12/13, 3/13) recovering u_AB. Reversed-order contrast confirmed: u_BA = -u_AB gives (-120, 360, -90) N, every component negated, establishing that the point order is part of the answer. Symbol continuity: u_AB, u_BA, r_AB, |r_AB| and the point coordinate names reused with identical meaning from unit_vector_along_line and position_vector_3d, with scalar F and F_vec introduced and F declared explicitly as a scalar magnitude distinct from the vector F bound by the moment skills; bare u not rebound.
